title: Genitive Forms: Singular, First patterns review
focus: Retrieve the taught genitive patterns in a mixed review.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: talo (“house”); koulu (“school”).
exercises.explanation: Keep talo and add -n: talo + n = talon. Keep koulu and add -n: koulu + n = koulun.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: katu (“street”); pankki (“bank”).
exercises.explanation: Change t to d: katu → kadu-; add -n to get kadun. Change kk to k: pankki → panki-; add -n to get pankin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: huone (“room”); vene (“boat”).
exercises.explanation: Lengthen e: huone → huonee-; add -n to get huoneen. Lengthen e: vene → venee-; add -n to get veneen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: nainen (“woman”); hevonen (“horse”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -nen with -se-: nai + se + n = naisen. Replace -nen with -se-: hevo + se + n = hevosen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: auto (“car”); koira (“dog”).
exercises.explanation: Keep auto and add -n: auto + n = auton. Keep koira and add -n: koira + n = koiran.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kauppa (“shop”); äiti (“mother”).
exercises.explanation: Change pp to p: kauppa → kaupa-; add -n to get kaupan. Change t to d and keep i: äiti → äidi-; add -n to get äidin.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: perhe (“family”); kone (“machine”).
exercises.explanation: Lengthen e: perhe → perhee-; add -n to get perheen. Lengthen e: kone → konee-; add -n to get koneen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: ihminen (“person”); suomalainen (“Finnish person”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -nen with -se-: ihmi + se + n = ihmisen. Replace -nen with -se-: suomalai + se + n = suomalaisen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: koulu (“school”); kirja (“book”).
exercises.explanation: Keep koulu and add -n: koulu + n = koulun. Keep kirja and add -n: kirja + n = kirjan.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: pankki (“bank”); leipä (“bread”).
exercises.explanation: Change kk to k: pankki → panki-; add -n to get pankin. Change p to v and keep ä: leipä → leivä-; add -n to get leivän.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: vene (“boat”); hame (“skirt”).
exercises.explanation: Lengthen e: vene → venee-; add -n to get veneen. Lengthen e: hame → hamee-; add -n to get hameen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: hevonen (“horse”); punainen (“red”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -nen with -se-: hevo + se + n = hevosen. Replace -nen with -se-: punai + se + n = punaisen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: koira (“dog”); pallo (“ball”).
exercises.explanation: Keep koira and add -n: koira + n = koiran. Keep pallo and add -n: pallo + n = pallon.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: äiti (“mother”); silta (“bridge”).
exercises.explanation: Change t to d and keep i: äiti → äidi-; add -n to get äidin. Change lt to ll: silta → silla-; add -n to get sillan.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kone (“machine”); kirje (“letter”).
exercises.explanation: Lengthen e: kone → konee-; add -n to get koneen. Lengthen e: kirje → kirjee-; add -n to get kirjeen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: suomalainen (“Finnish person”); iloinen (“happy”).
exercises.explanation: Replace -nen with -se-: suomalai + se + n = suomalaisen. Replace -nen with -se-: iloi + se + n = iloisen.
